a:r.a:t: Fatty Acid Oxidation Is Performed by a Single Trifunctional Protein

p:cNvPr.descr: An image depicting the enzymes of beta oxidation. Image (a) is the gram-positive bacteria and mitochondrial short-chain-specific system, and is, for the most part, a circle. It begins with a substrate attached to Enz1 in a pink image. After this arrow, it states, “Intermediate.” After this, an arrow points to Enz2 in a green image, which points to intermediate. An arrow follows this to Enz3 in a darker green image, which points to intermediate. An arrow follows this to Enz4 in a purple image, which points to product. Image (b) is gram-negative bacteria. A substrate is attached to Enz1, which points to Enz2, which points to Enz3, which points to Enz4, which points to product. All of the images touch each other. Image (c) is the mitochondrial very-long-chain-specific system. This matrix begins on the right, where the substrate is attached to Enz1, which points to Enz2, which points left to Enz3, which points left to Enz4, which points left to product. All of these images are on the inner membrane. Image (d) is the peroxisomal and glyoxysomal systems, which begins with Enz1 having the substrate attached, and pointing right to Enz2, which has an arrow pointing down to Enz3, which points to Enz4, which points to product. To the right of Enz2 is Enz6, where MFP points to it, To the right of Enz3 and below Enz6 is Enz5. These are all in various shades of green.
